issue_snapshot.title: The error message from PackageLoader could be more helpful
issue_snapshot.body:
When following [the basics of setting up jinja2](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.1.x/api/#basics), if you don't create the appropriate `templates` directory in your package, you get this error message:

```
ValueError: The 'mypackage' package was not installed in a way that PackageLoader understands.
```

This could be significantly improved by explaining the actual problem: The PackageLoader could not find a suitable "templates" directory.

To replicate, add this to `mypackage.py`:

```python
from jinja2 import Environment, PackageLoader


env = Environment(loader=PackageLoader("mypackage"))
```

If you run `python mypackage.py` you will see a traceback similar to this:

```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "mypackage/mypackage.py", line 4, in <module>
    env = Environment(loader=PackageLoader("mypackage"))
  File ".virtualenvs/mypackage/lib/python3.10/site-packages/jinja2/loaders.py", line 291, in __init__
    import_module(package_name)
  File ".pyenv/versions/3.10.3/lib/python3.10/importlib/__init__.py", line 126, in import_module
    return _bootstrap._gcd_import(name[level:], package, level)
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1050, in _gcd_import
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1027, in _find_and_load
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1006, in _find_and_load_unlocked
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 688, in _load_unlocked
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>", line 883, in exec_module
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 241, in _call_with_frames_removed
  File "mypackage/mypackage.py", line 4, in <module>
    env = Environment(loader=PackageLoader("mypackage"))
  File ".virtualenvs/mypackage/lib/python3.10/site-packages/jinja2/loaders.py", line 323, in __init__
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: The 'mypackage' package was not installed in a way that PackageLoader understands.

```

Seeing an error message that explained that jinja2 couldn't find an appropriate "templates" directory would be much better.

- Python version: 3.10.3

issue_snapshot.title: `logical_line` for call with f-string can result in invalid ast under Python 3.12
issue_snapshot.body:
### how did you install flake8?

```console
$ pip install flake8
```


### unmodified output of `flake8 --bug-report`

```json
{}
```


### describe the problem

#### what I expected to happen

Some of the plugins in [`hacking`](https://pypi.org/project/hacking) use a combo of `ast.parse` and `logical_line` to generate an AST for an individual line that is then fed into an `ast.NodeVisitor` subclass. These work just fine on Python 3.11 and earlier, but I've noticed they fail under specific circumstances on Python 3.12. I've included a minimal reproducer below. There's a chance I am "holding it wrong" but I'd like to confirm this first.

#### sample code

`test.py`

```python
import unittest


class TestFoo(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_foo(self):
        response_key = 'foo'
        response_val = 'bar'
        body_output = ''
        self.assertEqual(
            f'{{"{response_key}": "{response_val}"}}', body_output
        )
```

`checks.py`:

```
class NoneArgChecker(ast.NodeVisitor):
    def __init__(self, func_name, num_args=2):
        self.func_name = func_name
        self.num_args = num_args
        self.none_found = False

    def visit_Call(self, node):
        # snipped
        ...


def foo(logical_line, noqa):
    if noqa:
        return

    for func_name in (
        'assertEqual', 'assertIs', 'assertNotEqual', 'assertIsNot'
    ):
        try:
            start = logical_line.index('.%s(' % func_name) + 1
        except ValueError:
            continue
        checker = NoneArgChecker(func_name)
        # print(logical_line)
        checker.visit(ast.parse(logical_line))
        continue
        if checker.none_found:
            yield start, "H203: Use assertIs(Not)None to check for None"
```

`tox.ini`:

```ini
[flake8:local-plugins]
extension =
    X123 = checks:foo
paths = .
```

#### commands ran

```console
$ flake8 test.py
wow.py:1:23: E999 SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?
```

If I comment out the `print` statement, I see different results for Python 3.12 compared Pythons 3.10 and 3.11. Under 3.12:

```
self.assertEqual(f'x{x{response_key}xxxx{response_val}xx}', body_output)
```

Under 3.10 and 3.11:

```
self.assertEqual(f'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx', body_output)
```

### additional information

The E999 error is associated with line 1 of the file, despite the error actually coming from a plugin. This led me on a wild goose chase as I tried to figure out why flake8 thought my file was invalid Python but Python itself did not. I suspect this might also be user error and I should be handling the potential exception from `ast.parse` in my plugin but again, I just wanted to confirm that this was expected practice.

issue_snapshot.title: parse_url doesn't %-decode user/password
issue_snapshot.body:
### Subject

As far as I understand[^rfc], reserved characters need to %-encoded in URLs.

[^rfc]: [RFC 3986 section 3.2.1.](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.2.1): `userinfo    = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" )`

So, if you have user "u{er" with password "pa}}word" for example.com, you would encode it as `http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com`. However, parse_url doesn't decode those parts:

```py
>>> import urllib3
>>> urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com").auth
'u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword'
```

Even worse, it encodes them for invalid URLs if you try to work around it:

```py
>>> urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u{er:pass}}word@example.com").auth
'u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword'
```

Therefore, if you use it to parse an URL pass `url.auth` into `make_headers(basic_auth=url.auth)`, you get a 401 and a downtime (ask me how I know).


### Environment

```
OS macOS-26.4-x86_64-i386-64bit-Mach-O
Python 3.14.3
OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026
urllib3 2.6.3
```

### Steps to Reproduce

See above.

### Expected Behavior

`urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com").auth` should return `u{er:pa}}word`.

`yarl` and `httpx.URL` get this right.

### Actual Behavior

It returns `u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword`

issue_snapshot.title: `uv export --format cyclonedx1.5` omits component hashes that `uv.lock` already carries
issue_snapshot.body:
## Summary

The CycloneDX export emits no hashes for any component, even though `uv.lock` records `sha256` per sdist and per wheel by default and the `requirements.txt` export propagates them. `uv export --no-hashes` is documented as "Omit hashes in the generated output," which implies hashes are on by default. For `cyclonedx1.5` there are none to omit, so the flag is a no-op there.

## Platform

macOS 14 arm64

## Version

uv 0.12.4

## Reproduction

```console
$ uv init edgetest && cd edgetest
$ uv add requests

# uv.lock carries hashes
$ grep -c 'hash = "sha256:' uv.lock
184

# the requirements export propagates them
$ uv export --format requirements.txt --hashes | grep -c 'sha256:'
184

# the CycloneDX export does not, with or without --hashes
$ uv export --format cyclonedx1.5 | jq '[.components[] | select(.hashes)] | length'
0
$ uv export --format cyclonedx1.5 --hashes | jq '[.components[] | select(.hashes)] | length'
0

# and not on externalReferences either
$ uv export --format cyclonedx1.5 | jq '[.components[]? | (.externalReferences // [])[]? | select(.hashes)] | length'
0
```

The export emits every component without hashes:

```console
$ uv export --format cyclonedx1.5 | jq -c '.components[0]'
{"bom-ref":"certifi-2@2026.7.22","name":"certifi","type":"library",
 "purl":"pkg:pypi/certifi@2026.7.22","version":"2026.7.22", …}
```

The dependency graph, `purl`s, and the `uv:package:marker` properties are all present and correct. Hashes are the only lockfile data that does not survive.

## Expected

Components carry the hashes from `uv.lock`, in either place CycloneDX defines for them:

- `components[].hashes[]`, or
- a `hashes` array on the component's distribution `externalReference`.

`--no-hashes` should suppress them, matching its behavior for `requirements.txt`.

## Why it matters

Hashes are the field that makes an SBOM verifiable rather than merely descriptive. A consumer uses them to confirm the artifact they received is the artifact the SBOM describes. Published baselines ask for them explicitly:

- **CISA's 2026 Minimum Elements for an SBOM** (July 2026) lists Component Hash Value and Component Hash Algorithm among its 17 data fields.
- **OWASP SCVS V1.0 V2.18**: "Components defined in SBOM have one or more file hashes (SHA-256, SHA-512, etc)."

## Notes

- The hash issues that exist (#6944, #9225, #10987) all concern the `requirements.txt` export. Neither #6012 nor the implementing PR #16523 scopes hash support in or out.
